\section{Overview}
The low degree Fourier mass involving omitted coordinates is controlled by their influence threshold. The estimate permits endpoint noise rates and zero thresholds.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{lemma}[Fourier omission under an influence threshold]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.fourier_omission_le}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteNorms.weighted_lowDegree_omission_le, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.stableInfluence_le, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.expect_nonneg, BooleanAnalysis.fourierCoeff, BooleanAnalysis.influence, BooleanAnalysis.isPmOne, BooleanAnalysis.totalInfluence, KKL.noisyInfluence}
\difficulty{5}
Let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$ be a function on the uniform Boolean cube, $J\subseteq[n]$, $k\in\mathbb N$, $0\le\rho\le1$, and $\tau\ge0$. If $I_i(f)\le\tau$ for every $i\notin J$, then $\rho^k\sum_{|S|\le k,\ S\nsubseteq J}\widehat f(S)^2\le\tau^{(1-\rho)/(1+\rho)}I(f)$, with $0^0=1$. For a real cube function $h$, define $I_i(h)=\tfrac14\mathbb E_x(h(x)-h(x^{(i)}))^2$, where $x^{(i)}$ flips coordinate $i$ and $\mathbb E_x$ is uniform expectation, and $I(h)=\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}I_i(h)$.
\end{lemma}
